requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

result.summary:
Independent re-verification, fresh run superseding step-05-release-validator.json (which predated the post-rebase integration fix). Free memory checked before running (as low as ~530MB-650MB free of 33GB total mid-run, confirming the handoff's warning); ran mix test SERIAL (not scripts/test_parallel.sh) as instructed: 'Finished in 2749.4 seconds (28.3s async, 2721.0s sync)' / 'Result: 5048 passed (8 properties, 5040 tests), 27 excluded' -- zero failures, exit 0.

Also independently ran `mix letflow.check.test` (mandatory per this role's own instructions) twice. First run: 'Result: 374/375 passed' / 'Failed: 1 test', exit code from scripts/test_parallel.sh was 1 -- but the mix task's own `after` block (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex ~L211-215) deletes the partition-log tmp_dir immediately after reading it regardless of outcome, and my `tail -80` truncated the printed full-failure-detail block before I could read which test failed; the tmp_dir was gone by the time I went to inspect it directly. Re-ran a second time capturing full untruncated output: all 16 partitions '0 failures, exit 0', 5/5 isolated wasm_hang subprocess tests passed, and the isolated lua_wallclock_race run passed clean -- 'mix letflow.check.test: OK' on every stage. Combined with the serial mix test's clean 5048/5048, I conclude the single first-run failure was transient resource-contention noise under the critically-low free-memory conditions (consistent with this run's own documented memory pressure), not a real regression -- REQ-425 touches only apps/mobile/ (Flutter/Dart), never lib/letflow/ or priv/repo/migrations/, so it cannot be the backend cause of a flaky Elixir test either way. Flagging as an observation, not a blocker: docs/anti-patterns.md may be worth a note that mix letflow.check.test's own tmp_dir cleanup makes a first-run flake for-practical-purposes unattributable after the fact -- future runs under memory pressure should capture full (untruncated) output, not tail -N.

Ran `cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test` independently: `flutter analyze` -> 'No issues found! (ran in 5.9s)'. `flutter test` -> '+147 ... All tests passed!' (147 tests, matches TEST-RUNNER's own count), including test/guards/single_api_client_guard_test.dart's 6 tests (real-tree zero violations + 4 self-test fixtures) and test/api/api_client_test.dart + test/api/api_client_hardening_test.dart's 28 tests together.

Confirmed all 7 acceptance criteria directly against current code/tests (not against status-history narration):
AC1 (401 refresh-then-retry, concurrent share one refresh) -- apps/mobile/test/api/api_client_hardening_test.dart 'a 401 then 200 triggers exactly one refresh and exactly one retry' and 'two concurrent 401s trigger exactly one refresh total, each request still retried once', both passing; mechanism read directly in apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart's _RefreshCoordinator.refreshOnce (single _inFlightRefresh future shared by concurrent callers).
AC2 (refresh failure clears tokens, routes to login) -- 'refresh failure (AC2) refresh failure deletes the tenant's tokens from the secure store and routes to login' and the no-refresh-token variant, both passing; _RefreshCoordinator._handleFailure calls _tokenStore.delete then _routeToLogin().
AC3 (5xx backoff GET-only, bounded, POST never retried) -- '5xx backoff for GET only (AC3)' group: 503-twice-then-200 with increasing delays (200ms, 400ms) asserted directly against fake-adapter request count (hasLength(3)); 503-on-every-attempt asserts hasLength(kMaxServerRetryAttempts) (the named constant, =3) and ServerError(lastStatusCode:503); 'a POST receiving 503 is not retried' asserts hasLength(1) and zero delays. All passing.
AC4 (ApiError variant mapping incl. module-404 vs plain-404, 429 Retry-After) -- 'ApiError variant mapping (AC4)' group in api_client_hardening_test.dart covers every classifyError branch directly (403->ForbiddenError, 409->ConflictError, 400->ServerError catch-all, 404 module-path->ModuleNotAvailableError, 404 elsewhere->NotFoundError, 429 Retry-After:7->BackpressureError(7), 422->ValidationError with parsed RFC9457 field errors, malformed 422 body, connection-error DioException->NetworkUnavailableError); read api_error.dart's classifyError directly and confirmed the code matches every asserted mapping exactly, including the exact-rule module-path regex (bare /api/v1/modules/exam with no trailing segment does NOT count as module-scoped, also tested).
AC5 (no raw transport exception escapes lib/api/) -- 'no raw transport exception escapes lib/api/ (AC5)' group: a DioException/SocketException maps to NetworkUnavailableError never a raw DioException, and every ApiError variant is confirmed isA<Exception> and isNot(isA<DioException>()). Passing.
AC6 (static guard fails self-test fixture, passes real tree) -- read apps/mobile/test/guards/single_api_client_guard_test.dart directly: 4 self-test fixtures (dio import outside lib/api/, http import outside lib/api/, dart:io HttpClient outside lib/api/, dio import INSIDE lib/api/ exempted) all pass, plus the real-tree 'zero single-api-client-boundary violations' test passes -- this is also the guard whose earlier failure (dio import in the pre-fix pinned_form_resolver.dart) triggered the integration fix this recheck exists to re-verify.
AC7 (flutter analyze/test pass with real output, SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off) -- both quoted above; SECURITY-REVIEWER's own gate on this run passed on recheck2 (handoffs/WF02-REQ425-20260929/step-02c-security-reviewer-recheck2.json, result.status: PASS, after two FAILs on rework1/rework2 -- the cross-tenant refresh-race BLOCKERs, now covered by api_client_hardening_test.dart's 'cross-tenant refresh race' and 'cross-tenant retry-dispatch race' test groups, both passing).

Independently re-read apps/mobile/lib/definitions/pinned_form_resolver.dart in full (not trusting step-02d's REVIEWER characterization alone): the file now declares `final dynamic response;` inside the try block, a single `catch (_)` returning PinnedFormUnavailable(fetchFailed) for either a network exception or a thrown ApiError, no dio import, no statusCode check -- exactly as step-02b/02d describe. Independently re-verified the underlying claim that made the old branch dead: read apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart's _sendWithBackoff (lines ~465-515) and _handleUnauthorized (lines ~521-610) directly -- every code path either returns a response with a genuine 2xx statusCode or throws classifyError(...)/UnauthorizedError; ApiClient.get() can never return a non-2xx Response. The removed `if (response.statusCode != 200)` branch was therefore genuinely unreachable dead code; this is a no-public-behavior-change cleanup, confirmed first-hand.

Staleness check: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-425 entry (line 31549) still reads status: in_progress, acceptance_criteria unchanged and matching this handoff's task.acceptance_criteria verbatim. docs/status/requirement_status.v24.yaml (lines 281-296) has exactly one event for REQ-425 (started, agent: ORCH, 2026-09-29T11:21:12Z) -- no done/verified event yet, consistent with 'DOC-UPDATER, next, flips it to done.' No staleness found.
issues: Observation (non-blocking): mix letflow.check.test's own tmp_dir cleanup (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex's after-block File.rm_rf!) runs unconditionally right after reading the partition logs into stdout, so a first-run flake under a truncated (tail -N) capture becomes unattributable after the fact -- the raw partition log is gone by the time a reader goes to inspect it directly. This run's own first check.test attempt hit exactly this (374/375 passed, 1 test failed, detail lost to a tail -80 pipe); a clean full-output re-run (all 16 partitions 0 failures) plus the serial mix test's independent clean 5048/5048 support treating it as transient resource-contention noise under this run's documented critical memory pressure, not a real regression -- but this is inference, not a direct read of the failing test's own assertion. REQ-425 cannot be its root cause either way (apps/mobile/ only, no lib/letflow/ or priv/repo/migrations/ changes). Worth a docs/anti-patterns.md entry for a future run: capture mix letflow.check.test's full output, never tail -N, especially under memory pressure.
